## First: what I had to assume The repo contents weren't included with the task — I only received the canonical scenario spec, not the actual `overlays/*/kustomization.yaml` or the CRs under `clusters/` and `infra/`. So the patches below target **placeholder identifiers**. Everything in this table must be reconciled against your actual manifests before this merges; the patch *structure* is correct, the `name:`/`group:` values are guesses. | What I assumed | Where it's used | Confirm by | |---|---|---| | App is a plain `apps/v1` Deployment named `web-app` (not a `HelmRelease`) | Patch 1 | `kustomize build overlays/prod \| yq 'select(.kind=="Deployment").metadata.name'` | | AWS resources are Crossplane `provider-aws` CRs (`RDSInstance`, `Bucket`) | Patches 2–4 | `grep -r "aws.crossplane.io\|services.k8s.aws" infra/ clusters/` | | RDS claim named `app-db`, bucket named `app-assets` | Patches 2–4 | same | | Base sets `replicas: 2` and `dbInstanceClass: db.t3.micro` explicitly | `op: replace` semantics | `kustomize build overlays/dev \| grep -E 'replicas\|dbInstanceClass'` | If you're on ACK instead of Crossplane, see the field mapping in section 5 — the field names differ, the approach doesn't. --- ## 1. `overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml` Keep every line that's already in your file (`namespace`, `resources`, `images`, `labels`, generators…). Add only the `patches:` block. If a `patches:` key already exists, append to it rather than creating a second one. ```yaml apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1 kind: Kustomization # ---- existing content, unchanged — shown for context only ---- namespace: prod resources: - ../../clusters/prod - ../../infra # images:, labels:, configMapGenerator: ... leave exactly as they are # -------------------------------------------------------------- patches: # (1) App replicas: 2 -> 4 - target: group: apps version: v1 kind: Deployment name: web-app patch: | - op: replace path: /spec/replicas value: 4 # (2)(3) RDS: db.t3.micro -> db.t3.medium, single-AZ -> multi-AZ - target: group: database.aws.crossplane.io version: v1beta1 kind: RDSInstance name: app-db patch: | - op: replace path: /spec/forProvider/dbInstanceClass value: db.t3.medium # 'add' not 'replace': dev almost certainly omits multiAZ entirely, # and RFC 6902 'replace' fails on an absent member while 'add' # upserts. Do NOT switch this to 'replace' without checking base. - op: add path: /spec/forProvider/multiAZ value: true # (4) S3 cross-region replication to us-west-2. # Strategic-merge here rather than JSON patch: the nested block is far more # readable, and we want to create the whole replicationConfiguration subtree # in one go (a JSON patch would need a create-parent-then-append dance). - target: group: s3.aws.crossplane.io version: v1beta1 kind: Bucket name: app-assets patch: | apiVersion: s3.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1 kind: Bucket metadata: name: app-assets spec: forProvider: # Replication REQUIRES versioning on source and destination. # Asserted here even though base should already set it — cheap idempotent guard. versioningConfiguration: status: Enabled replicationConfiguration: role: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/app-assets-replication rules: - id: crr-us-west-2 status: Enabled priority: 0 filter: prefix: "" deleteMarkerReplication: status: Enabled destination: bucket: arn:aws:s3:::app-assets-prod-usw2 storageClass: STANDARD ``` --- ## 2. The part that cannot live in that one file **Requirement 4 is not satisfiable by editing only `overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml`.** S3 CRR is not a flag — it's a reference to two objects that must already exist: 1. a **destination bucket in us-west-2** (versioning enabled), and 2. an **IAM role** the source bucket assumes, with `s3:GetReplicationConfiguration`/`ListBucket` on the source and `s3:ReplicateObject`/`ReplicateDelete`/`ReplicateTags` on the destination. Kustomize patches can only mutate resources that are already in the resource graph; there is no syntax for declaring a new resource inline in `kustomization.yaml`. So one of these is true: - **A — those resources already exist in `infra/`.** Then the file above is complete: replace the two hardcoded ARNs with the real ones (or `roleRef`/`bucketRef` if your provider-aws version supports cross-resource references, which is preferable to hardcoded ARNs). Check first: `grep -ri "replication\|us-west-2" infra/ clusters/`. - **B — they don't exist.** Then you must add a file. I'd add it *inside the prod overlay* — `overlays/prod/s3-replication-target.yaml` — and reference it from `resources:`. This deviates from the letter of "only modify `overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml`" but preserves its actual intent: the file sits under `overlays/prod/`, dev's kustomization never references it, so `kustomize build overlays/dev` is byte-identical. Putting these in `infra/` instead would leak a us-west-2 bucket and a replication role into dev.
Path B: overlays/prod/s3-replication-target.yaml + kustomization delta ```yaml # overlays/prod/s3-replication-target.yaml apiVersion: s3.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1 kind: Bucket metadata: name: app-assets-prod-usw2 spec: forProvider: locationConstraint: us-west-2 versioningConfiguration: status: Enabled serverSideEncryptionConfiguration: rules: - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault: sseAlgorithm: AES256 publicAccessBlockConfiguration: blockPublicAcls: true blockPublicPolicy: true ignorePublicAcls: true restrictPublicBuckets: true providerConfigRef: name: aws-prod --- apiVersion: iam.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1 kind: Role metadata: name: app-assets-replication spec: forProvider: assumeRolePolicyDocument: | {"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow", "Principal":{"Service":"s3.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]} providerConfigRef: name: aws-prod --- apiVersion: iam.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1 kind: Policy metadata: name: app-assets-replication spec: forProvider: name: app-assets-replication document: | {"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[ {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetReplicationConfiguration","s3:ListBucket"], "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::app-assets-prod"}, {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication","s3:GetObjectVersionAcl","s3:GetObjectVersionTagging"], "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::app-assets-prod/*"}, {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:ReplicateObject","s3:ReplicateDelete","s3:ReplicateTags"], "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::app-assets-prod-usw2/*"}]} providerConfigRef: name: aws-prod --- apiVersion: iam.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1 kind: RolePolicyAttachment metadata: name: app-assets-replication spec: forProvider: roleName: app-assets-replication policyArnRef: name: app-assets-replication providerConfigRef: name: aws-prod ``` Then in `overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml`: ```yaml resources: - ../../clusters/prod - ../../infra - s3-replication-target.yaml # prod-only; dev never references this path ``` Note the policy is scoped to two specific bucket ARNs — no wildcard actions, per acceptance criterion 4.
--- ## 3. Why these patch types - **JSON 6902 for scalars.** A one-line typo in a strategic-merge patch against a CRD is a silent no-op; `op: replace` against a wrong path is a hard failure at build time. For `dbInstanceClass` and `replicas` — where "silently still db.t3.micro in prod" is the expensive outcome — I want the loud version. - **Strategic merge for the replication subtree.** Readability, and it creates missing parent maps for free. - **Caveat on merge semantics with CRDs:** kustomize has no strategic-merge metadata for CRD schemas, so it falls back to JSON merge patch — **lists are replaced wholesale, not merged by key**. Here that's what we want (`rules` is fully specified). But if you later patch a list that base also populates (e.g. `tags`), expect replacement, not append. - **`replicas:` transformer:** for change 1, kustomize's built-in `replicas:` field is arguably more idiomatic than a patch. The task specified patches, so I used one. Either is fine; don't use both. - **Deprecated fields:** if your file still uses `patchesStrategicMerge:` / `patchesJson6902:`, migrate to the unified `patches:` above (kustomize ≥ v4.5.2; Flux's kustomize-controller is well past that). --- ## 4. Proving dev is untouched The constraint isn't "don't edit dev's file" — it's "dev's rendered output and reconciled state don't move." Verify both: ```bash # render dev BEFORE your edit git stash kustomize build overlays/dev > /tmp/dev-before.yaml git stash pop # render dev AFTER kustomize build overlays/dev > /tmp/dev-after.yaml diff -u /tmp/dev-before.yaml /tmp/dev-after.yaml # MUST be empty # confirm prod actually changed kustomize build overlays/prod | grep -E 'replicas:|dbInstanceClass|multiAZ|replicationConfiguration' -A2 # server-side, against the live cluster (Flux) flux diff kustomization prod --path ./overlays/prod flux diff kustomization dev --path ./overlays/dev # expect "no changes" ``` Two things to check that are outside the two overlay files: - **Flux `Kustomization` objects must be independent.** Separate `spec.path`, separate `sourceRef`/target namespaces, `prune: true` on each. If dev and prod are reconciled by one `Kustomization` with a shared path, or share a `dependsOn` that spans both, overlay hygiene won't save you. - **Don't trust kustomize to fail on a missed target.** Behaviour when a `target:` selector matches nothing has varied across versions — a renamed Deployment could leave you at `replicas: 2` with a green build. Add a CI assertion instead: ```bash # fails the build if prod didn't actually get the values kustomize build overlays/prod | yq -e ' (select(.kind=="Deployment" and .metadata.name=="web-app").spec.replicas == 4) and (select(.kind=="RDSInstance").spec.forProvider.dbInstanceClass == "db.t3.medium") and (select(.kind=="RDSInstance").spec.forProvider.multiAZ == true)' # fails the build if a "prod-only" PR moved dev kustomize build overlays/dev | sha256sum -c dev.sha256 ``` --- ## 5. Field mapping if you're not on Crossplane provider-aws | Change | Crossplane `provider-aws` | ACK (`*.services.k8s.aws`) | |---|---|---| | Instance class | `spec.forProvider.dbInstanceClass` | `spec.dbInstanceClass` | | Multi-AZ | `spec.forProvider.multiAZ` | `spec.multiAZ` | | Bucket replication | `spec.forProvider.replicationConfiguration` | `spec.replication` (`role` + `rules[]`) | | Group/version | `database.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1`, `s3.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1` | `rds.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1`, `s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1` | If the app is a `HelmRelease` rather than a Deployment, patch 1 becomes a target on `helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v2` `HelmRelease` with `path: /spec/values/replicaCount` (confirm the key name in the chart's `values.yaml` — `replicaCount` vs `replicas` vs `autoscaling.minReplicas`; if HPA is enabled, patching replicas is a no-op and you want the HPA bounds instead). --- ## 6. Gaps worth a follow-up ticket Out of scope for this change, but the spec's acceptance criteria imply these and I can't verify them without the repo: - **RDS:** `deletionProtection: true`, `backupRetentionPeriod: ≥ 7`, `storageEncrypted: true`, `publiclyAccessible: false`. If base doesn't set these, prod is non-compliant regardless of instance class. `storageEncrypted` in particular **cannot be toggled in place** — flipping it on an existing instance forces a replace (snapshot + restore), so it needs a planned migration, not a patch. - **Multi-AZ conversion** is online but triggers a failover-class event and a sustained storage sync; schedule it, and confirm `db.t3.medium` clears any minimum-class requirement for your engine version. - **Enabling CRR replicates nothing retroactively.** Existing objects need an S3 Batch Replication job. Easy to ship this, see "replication enabled," and discover months later the destination only has post-cutover objects. - **Destination encryption:** if the source uses KMS rather than AES-256, add `destination.encryptionConfiguration.replicaKmsKeyID` (a us-west-2 key) and `sourceSelectionCriteria.sseKmsEncryptedObjects.status: Enabled`, plus `kms:Decrypt`/`kms:Encrypt` on the replication role.
